best_season: Late September through mid-October, when the face has consolidated into firm neve/ice before winter storms bury or destabilize it — described as best 'before the first snow storms arrive.'

season: Late June to early October, once Eightmile Road is open and the high snow has consolidated or melted
best_season: July to September. Early season brings steep, hard snow on the gullies and notches (axe and crampons needed); late summer is mostly dry rock and talus.

season: Jul-Sep (summer); winter ascents documented but far more serious
Jul-Oct, with late Sep/early Oct favored for larch color and stable weather

best_season: A cold window in May is the consensus best time: long days, a stable and still-continuous snowpack, and a bergschrund that has not yet opened. Reports consistently warn that waiting until June is problematic because the schrund opens rapidly. Early May trips have found powder rather than ice on the headwall. Winter ascents have been made (January and early May are both documented) but require biking or skiing in from the SR 20 closure gate and full avalanche, cornice and crevasse competence. This route is emphatically not a late-summer objective.

Snow-covered conditions (roughly May-July) make the Pride Glacier crossing and ridge travel most straightforward with axe and crampons; by later summer the glacier is barer and more crevassed while the rock band is dry but still exposed.

season: Jun-Jul (early season preferred, before the moat opens)
Jul-Aug (only documented ascent was late July; a long, low-elevation brush approach and 'easy snow' finish likely bias the feasible window)
Jun-Sep (rock stays in condition all summer once the approach is snow-free)
Aug-Sep (documented ascents; snow may linger on the approach gully earlier in summer)
May-Jun (continuous snow climb; likely melts out by late summer)
Jun-Sep (snow can persist on the connecting ridges into early summer)
best_season: Summer, after snow on the connecting ridges has consolidated or melted; a June ascent in trip reports required an ice axe and mountaineering-level snow travel, so early-season parties should expect firmer snow conditions on Mastiff's and Howard's ridges.

season: Jul-Oct (documented ascents span July through early October)
best_season: Trip reports document ascents from mid-July through early October; the route is a popular add-on for parties in Crescent Creek Basin climbing Terror, Himmelhorn, or the McMillan Spires.

season: Jun-Sep (snow lingers into Jul in the summit gully)
best_season: Most commonly climbed June through September. Snow can linger in the summit gully into July, favoring an ice axe and sometimes crampons/microspikes for security; a documented winter ascent (probable first winter ascent, Feb 9, 2020) shows the route is feasible outside summer but adds cornices, avalanche-prone couloir terrain, and a much longer snowed-in road approach.
Best from mid-summer into early fall (roughly July-September); the Boulder River Wilderness holds snow at elevation into July and can see new snow return by October, per USFS trail data.
